title: NOBLE VILLAGE BOARD
full_story:
Village Clerk Cindy Manuel reported that the Health and Safety binder is now complete and all employees have received training, and all documentation has been submitted to the Illinois Department of Labor, Illinois OSHA, and Rusty Miller, Public Safety Inspector.  All OSHA abatement documents have been accepted, and no further action is required.

The board discussed that the fee for the water salesman service has not been increased in several years and that a substantial increase was necessary.  The Board agreed to raise the fee by $2.00, making the new rate $3.00 per one hundred gallons, effective May 1st.

A motion was made by Trustee Ashley Pipher to approve road closures for the block of North Noble Avenue between Elm and Poplar Streets for the Freedom Festival on June 27th and the Noble Chowder on August 8th, including North Noble Avenue, Wildcat Street, and the 100 block of East Elm.

It was reported to the board that storm cleanup at the park has been completed.  An insurance adjuster assessed the damage, and the Village is awaiting further information from RMA regarding the claim.  A representative from Security Alarm will be onsite tomorrow, to review the village video system and provide information on possibly taking over the maintenance.

Residents were reminded that the Village of Noble Clean-Up Day is scheduled for April 29th.  The May Fest Car Show will be held on May 2nd, at the Noble Park and village-wide garage sales are scheduled for May 16th.

title: SCHOOL EVACUATED
full_story:
An accident involving a semi carrying anhydrous ammonia forced the evacuation of Johnsonville grade school on Tuesday afternoon.

The semi, operated by Dabney Trucking of Dixon Illinois missed its turn in front of the Johnsonville School, causing the rear wheels of the tanker to drop off into a ditch.  Out of an abundance of caution, the school was evacuated around lunch time, with all students being transported to Cisne Middle School.

Charlie Heck’s Towing and Recovery of Mt. Vernon was called to scene to lift the loaded tanker safely back onto the roadway. Students were returned to Johnsonville School at around 1:45 pm.

No injuries were reported and no anhydrous ammonia leaked from the tanker.

title: BLOOD DRIVE
full_story:
With a Blood Emergency in place throughout the Midwest, the American Red Cross is asking area blood donors to get out and give blood at their next earliest opportunity.

In response to the critical need for blood, the American Red Cross will have a blood drive today from Noon to 5 pm at the Flora Church of the Nazarene.

Donors, especially those with type O blood and those giving platelets, can help bolster the blood supply now by making an appointment to give in the coming weeks.  Make an appointment to donate by downloading the free Red Cross Blood Donor App, visiting redcrossblood.org or calling 1-800-RED CROSS (1-800-733-2767).  A donor card, driver’s license, or two forms of ID are required at check-in.

Those who give blood or platelets at this drive will get a $15 e-gift card to the merchant of their choice.

After todays drive the next Blood drives in our area will be on Tuesday at the Floyd Henson JR High from 3 to 7 pm and then on Tuesday, April 28th at the Flora High School from 8:30 am till 2 pm.

title: TRIAL DATE VACATED
full_story:
The trial date for a Vandalia murder suspect has been vacated.

Arnold Rivera Jr. faces multiple charges including first degree murder in the death last November of a Vandalia teenager.  The 43-year-old Rivera is also charged with aggravated criminal sexual assault and concealing a homicidal death.

Yesterday was the date for the final pre-trial hearing in Rivera’s case.  The judge in the case has delayed the case until May 5th.

The contention of extended media coverage will be considered by Judge Allan Lolie.  A possible plea might also be considered at the May 5th hearing.  Rivera remains in custody.

title: CHAMBER GOLF SCRAMBLE
full_story:
The Flora Chamber of Commerce is now accepting sponsorships for their 28th annual golf scramble to be held on Friday, June 5th.

The Chamber offers a variety of sponsorship opportunities to suit every budget.  From Gold Sponsorship at $400 to the affordable Bronze Sponsorship at $50, there’s an option for everyone to get involved and showcase their support for the Flora business community.

Team registration is $50 per person or $200 per team.  Entry fee includes 4 drink tickets courtesy of the Flora Bank and Trust a goodie bag with a sleeve of balls and lunch courtesy of the Flora Savings Bank.  There will also be mulligans, 4 foot strings, yellow tee boxes, for $20 each or $50 for all 3.

Check-in will begin at 11:30 am inside the Clubhouse, lunch is at Noon, and tee-time at 1:00pm.

To register your team call Arriel Dulaney at the Flora Chamber of Commerce at 618-662-5646.

title: GIRL SCOUT TOP SELLER
full_story:
Girl Scouts of Southern Illinois (GSofSI) would like to congratulate the Top Cookie Sellers from the annual Girl Scout Cookie Program for 2026.  Autumn Moody from the Clay County Service Unit sold 892 packages.

Girl Scouts made door-to-door sales, hosted cookie booths, and even made online sales to friends and family near and far. GSofSI recognizes the girls who sold the most packages for their Service Unit.

The Girl Scout Cookie Program helps girls gain five valuable life skills; goal setting, decision making, money management, people skills, and business ethics; that will benefit them throughout their lives.  Proceeds from these programs stay local to provide numerous opportunities for girls to explore their interests, become tomorrow’s leaders and change the world.

Girl Scouts and cookies share a rich history.  While recipes and box designs have changed over the years, selling cookies remains an important part of today’s Girl Scout program.  The activity of selling cookies is directly related to Girl Scouts’ purpose of helping all girls reach their full potential and helping them become strong, confident, and resourceful citizens.

The Girl Scout Cookie Program is the largest girl-led entrepreneurial program in the world.  Many successful businesswomen today say they got their start selling Girl Scout Cookies.  During cookie activities, girls are members of a team working toward a common goal, with each girl striving to do her best.

Girl Scouts of Southern Illinois serves over 6,300 girls and engages nearly 3,600 adults in 40 counties in Southern Illinois.  Adult volunteers and girls in K-12 are welcome.  Call 800-345-6858 or email [email protected].  Girl Scouts of Southern Illinois is a not-for-profit organization supported by various United Ways, businesses, and individual donors throughout the region.

title: BALLOON FEST TO MOVE
full_story:
The Greater Centralia Chamber of Commerce made a final decision to move Balloon Fest to Fairview Park for August 21st, 22nd, and 23rd.  With the move, the event will be free to attend.

In making the announcement, the chamber tried to answer some concerns.  They note that the size of Fairview Park is very similar to the area used at Foundation Park.  No vehicles of any kind will be allowed into Fairview Park, with free parking available at Fairview Park Plaza.  West Broadway from Buena Vista to Brooks Street will be closed to traffic during event hours.

The goal will be to have the same number of craft vendors, food vendors, and hot air balloons.  The event would still include Friday and Saturday night glows.  For the evening flights, some balloons would launch from Fairview Park, and others from surrounding areas, to fly over the park.  Even if all 35 hot air balloons could fit in Fairview Park, they do not plan to have all of them take off from the park for traffic and safety reasons.  All events are weather permitting.

There is still a possibility that Balloon Fest could return to Foundation Park in a future year.  The chamber says there are electrical issues, some of which may be corrected in a timely manner.  There are other concerns that need attention by the chamber, but those things take time to plan, budget, and implement.  The chamber will continue to meet with the Centralia Foundation Board that owns Foundation Park.

The chamber is thanking the City of Centralia for being so welcoming of the event and doing everything in their power to ensure Balloon Fest stays in Centralia.  With such short notice, the city has done everything in its power to make sure the transition to Fairview Park is as smooth as possible.  The chamber has been in touch with Centralia Police, Fire, ESDA, and Public Works to plan a safe Balloon Fest.

title: CDL REIMBURSEMENT PROGRAM
full_story:
In an effort to address the growing need for CDL truck drivers in the Illinois Basin oil production industry, the Illinois Petroleum Resource Board (IPRB) will be offering a CDL training/certification cost reimbursement program to oil production companies that are contributing to the IPRB assessment.

IPRB will reimburse qualifying companies for expenses up to $2,500 per employee seeking a CDL license.  Eligible expenses include training or schooling fees, required medical exams, DMV testing fees, and truck rental or access fees.  Companies will be required to submit proof of CDL license obtained, current employment at the company and receipts for any training or schooling, medical test fee and DMV test fee to qualify for reimbursement.

Text or call IPRB executive director Seth Whitehead at 618-367-4751 if you are a qualifying company that is interested.

title: NEW CANINE TRAINING FACILITY
full_story:
The Illinois State Police (ISP) and Capital Development Board (CDB) broke ground last week on a new canine training complex.  The $8.9 million state investment consists of two new buildings, including upgraded kennels, training areas, and office space.

With steady and supportive funding from the Pritzker administration and the General Assembly, the ISP canine training facilities, which support law enforcement agencies across the state, will be upgraded for the first time in decades.

“The Illinois State Police Academy provides the best training to our officers, and the new canine training complex will ensure our canine partners receive the best training as well,” said ISP Director Brendan F. Kelly.  “As our focus has expanded from traffic to trafficking, we’ve increased the tools in our toolbox, including the use of canines.  Our canine partners are integral in our work to combat crime, conduct search and rescue missions, and protect the public.”

As methods used by criminals have evolved in recent years, ISP has responded by incorporating new technology and techniques to combat crime, including the increased use of canines.  ISP provides a 10-week, full-service canine training course to both ISP Troopers, as well as local law enforcement agencies.  Included in those 10 weeks, canines are trained to track human odors.  This allows canines to locate criminals attempting to evade arrest and help in missing persons cases.  ISP currently has 64 canine teams that assist with missing person searches, drug and gun interdiction, officer protection, and evidence recovery.  In 2025, ISP canines assisted in almost 100 criminal apprehensions, 225 searches for items, more than 330 building searches (narcotics, person, explosives), almost 200 stolen vehicle recoveries, 117 firearm seizures, and the seizure of more than 3,600 pounds in illegal drugs.

Upgrades to the canine training complex include construction of an administrative building with office space for up to 80 personnel and additional classroom areas, as well as a kennel that can house up to 20 canines and allow for both indoor and outdoor training.

WSP is serving as the architectural and engineering firm for the project, with CAD Construction leading as the General Contractor.  CDB will oversee the project, providing management and oversight throughout construction in accordance with the protocol for state-funded projects.

“Supporting our sister agencies and their operational needs through strategic infrastructure investments is central to our mission,” said TJ Edwards, Executive Director of the Illinois Capital Development Board.  “CDB is proud to partner with ISP to deliver new facilities that enhance their training environments.”

CDB is also managing a separate project currently in design to renovate the pistol and rifle ranges at the Pawnee site, further supporting long-term improvements to ISP training infrastructure.  These efforts reflect the state’s commitment to modernizing facilities that improve public safety.
